models_evaluated: machine-learning survival models trained on SEER
machine-learning survival models trained on NCDB

links.outcome: AUC on internal versus external validation across databases
links.effect: Internal AUC 0.90-0.93; external AUC fell to 0.56-0.67 (NCDB models on SEER 0.67/0.60; SEER models on NCDB 0.61/0.56).
links.quote: However, external validation revealed poor transferability: NCDB models tested on SEER data achieved an AUC of 0.67 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.68) and 0.60 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.62), while SEER models tested on NCDB data achieved 0.61 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.62) and 0.56 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.58).

links.outcome: Performance of models on data from a different database/population than training
links.effect: Cross-database AUCs of 0.56-0.67 versus internal >0.90, described as poor and unsuitable for clinical decision-making.
links.quote: This dramatic performance drop demonstrates that models cannot be reliably transferred between different healthcare databases.

links.outcome: Generalization of models to a new population/data context
links.effect: External validation AUC <0.70 (0.56-0.67) vs internal 0.90-0.93, indicating failure to generalize.
links.quote: Cross-database application of models leads to poor predictive performance and should be avoided without revalidation.

links.effect: Internal AUCs were 0.93/0.91 (NCDB) and 0.90/0.92 (SEER); external AUCs were 0.67/0.60 and 0.61/0.56.
links.quote: However, external validation revealed poor transferability: NCDB models tested on SEER data achieved an AUC of 0.67 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.68) and 0.60 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.62), while SEER models tested on NCDB data achieved 0.61 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.62) and 0.56 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.58).

links.effect: External validation AUC values were < 0.70: NCDB-to-SEER 0.67/0.60; SEER-to-NCDB 0.61/0.56.
links.quote: Cross-database application of models leads to poor predictive performance and should be avoided without revalidation.

links.outcome: external validation discrimination versus internal validation
links.effect: Internal validation AUC was 0.90-0.93, but external validation dropped to 0.60-0.67 (NCDB on SEER) and 0.56-0.61 (SEER on NCDB).
links.quote: However, external validation revealed poor transferability: NCDB models tested on SEER data achieved an AUC of 0.67 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.68) and 0.60 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.62), while SEER models tested on NCDB data achieved 0.61 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.62) and 0.56 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.58).

links.outcome: model discrimination when transferred to external database population
links.effect: AUC values dropped below 0.70 upon external validation, indicating poor predictive performance when extending models across databases.
links.quote: These external validation AUC values < 0.70 indicate poor predictive performance (barely better than chance and unsuitable for clinical decision-making).

screen.practice: local validation on the target database before use
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the practice and necessity of external validation across differing registry databases, demonstrating severe performance drop (generalizability failure) when predictive models trained on one dataset (SEER or NCDB) are applied to another.

primary.practice: cross-database external validation / local validation before deployment
